source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע הַכְּנַעֲנִ֤י מֶֽלֶךְ־עֲרָד֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַנֶּ֔גֶב כִּ֚י בָּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל דֶּ֖רֶךְ הָאֲתָרִ֑ים וַיִּלָּ֨חֶם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּ֥שְׁבְּ׀מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שֶֽׁבִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard the Canaanite, king of Arad, dwelling [in] the Negev, that had come Israel [by the] way of the Atharim; and he fought against Israel and took captive from it captive[s].

en.L: And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel had come by the way of Atharim; and he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
en.B: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the Atharim road, he attacked Israel and took some of them prisoner.
en.R: The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the Negev, the dry country in the south. He heard that Israel was coming along the Atharim road. So he attacked the Israelites and captured some of them.

es.L: Y oyó el cananeo, el rey de Arad, que habitaba en el Néguev, que Israel había venido por el camino de Atarim; y peleó contra Israel y tomó de él cautivos.
es.B: Cuando el rey cananeo de Arad, que vivía en el Néguev, oyó que Israel avanzaba por el camino de Atarim, atacó a Israel y se llevó prisioneros a algunos de ellos.
es.R: El rey cananeo de Arad vivía en el Néguev, la región seca del sur. Supo que Israel venía por el camino de Atarim. Entonces atacó a los israelitas y capturó a algunos de ellos.

fr.L: Et le Cananéen, roi d’Arad, qui habitait le Néguev, entendit dire qu’Israël était venu par le chemin d’Atharim ; et il combattit contre Israël et en emmena quelques-uns captifs.
fr.B: Le roi cananéen d’Arad, qui habitait le Néguev, apprit qu’Israël arrivait par la route d’Atharim. Il attaqua Israël et fit des prisonniers parmi eux.
fr.R: Le roi cananéen d’Arad vivait dans le Néguev, la région sèche du sud. Il a appris qu’Israël arrivait par la route d’Atharim. Alors il a attaqué les Israélites et en a capturé quelques-uns.

sw.L: Naye Mkanaani, mfalme wa Aradi, aliyekaa Negebu, akasikia kwamba Israeli amekuja kwa njia ya Atharimu; akapigana na Israeli, akachukua baadhi yao mateka.
sw.B: Mfalme Mkanaani wa Aradi, aliyeishi Negebu, aliposikia kwamba Israeli walikuwa wakija kwa njia ya Atharimu, aliwashambulia Israeli, akawateka baadhi yao.
sw.R: Mfalme Mkanaani wa Aradi aliishi Negebu, nchi kavu ya kusini. Alisikia kwamba Waisraeli walikuwa wakija kwa njia ya Atharimu. Basi akawashambulia Waisraeli, akawateka baadhi yao.

vi.L: Và người Ca-na-an, vua A-rát, sống tại Nê-ghép, nghe rằng Y-sơ-ra-ên đã đến theo đường A-tha-rim; và vua giao chiến với Y-sơ-ra-ên và bắt một số người làm tù binh.
vi.B: Khi vua người Ca-na-an ở A-rát, sống tại miền Nê-ghép, nghe tin Y-sơ-ra-ên đang đi theo đường A-tha-rim, vua tấn công Y-sơ-ra-ên và bắt một số người làm tù binh.
vi.R: Vua người Ca-na-an ở A-rát sống tại miền Nê-ghép, là miền đất khô ở phía nam. Vua nghe tin dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đang đi theo đường A-tha-rim. Vì vậy vua tấn công dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và bắt một số người đem đi.

ko.L: 그리고 네겝에 살던 가나안 사람 아랏 왕이 이스라엘이 아다림 길로 왔다는 것을 들었다. 그리고 그가 이스라엘과 싸워 그들 가운데서 포로를 사로잡아 갔다.
ko.B: 네겝에 살던 가나안 사람 아랏 왕은 이스라엘이 아다림 길로 오고 있다는 소식을 듣고 이스라엘을 공격하여, 그들 가운데 몇 사람을 포로로 잡아갔다.
ko.R: 가나안 사람인 아랏 왕은 남쪽의 메마른 땅 네겝에 살고 있었다. 그는 이스라엘이 아다림 길로 오고 있다는 소식을 들었다. 그래서 그는 이스라엘 사람들을 공격하여 그들 가운데 몇 사람을 사로잡아 갔다.

pt.L: E o cananeu, o rei de Arade, que habitava no Neguebe, ouviu que Israel vinha pelo caminho de Atarim; e lutou contra Israel e levou alguns deles cativos.
pt.B: Quando o rei cananeu de Arade, que vivia no Neguebe, ouviu que Israel vinha pelo caminho de Atarim, atacou Israel e fez alguns deles prisioneiros.
pt.R: O rei cananeu de Arade vivia no Neguebe, a região seca do sul. Ele ouviu que Israel vinha pelo caminho de Atarim. Então atacou os israelitas e capturou alguns deles.

am.L: በኔጌብ ይኖር የነበረው ከነዓናዊው የዓራድ ንጉሥ እስራኤል በአታሪም መንገድ እንደ መጣ ሰማ፤ ከእስራኤልም ጋር ተዋጋ፤ ከእነርሱም ምርኮ ማረከ።
am.B: በኔጌብ ይኖር የነበረው ከነዓናዊው የዓራድ ንጉሥ እስራኤል በአታሪም መንገድ እንደሚመጣ በሰማ ጊዜ እስራኤልን ወጋ፤ ከእነርሱም አንዳንዶቹን ማረከ።
am.R: ከነዓናዊው የዓራድ ንጉሥ በደቡብ ባለው ደረቅ ምድር በኔጌብ ይኖር ነበር። እስራኤል በአታሪም መንገድ እንደሚመጣ ሰማ። ስለዚህ እስራኤላውያንን ወግቶ ከእነርሱ አንዳንዶቹን ማረከ።

decisions.choice: Arad in the Negev: a Canaanite town in the dry south of the land
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry country south of the hill country of Judah. Arad lay in its northern part (Joshua 12:14; Judges 1:16). Its king blocked Israel's way into the land from the south, where Israel had been beaten back before (14:44-45).

decisions.choice: the way of Atharim: a road named after a place, Atharim
decisions.reason: Atharim is read here as a place name, a road known by the place it led to. The word is found nowhere else, and it could also be read as "the way of the spies", the route the spies took into the land (13:17-21). The place cannot be located today.

decisions.choice: the Canaanite, the king of Arad: one man, the king
decisions.reason: "The Canaanite" and "king of Arad" name the same person: the king is the subject of "heard", "fought" and "took captive". In 33:40 the same king is named again. "Canaanite" here is a general name for the people of the land.

decisions.choice: the dry country in the south
decisions.reason: Readable explains the place name Negev, which many readers will not know.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("entendit", "attaqua"); passé composé at Readable ("a appris", "a attaqué")
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Pentateuch: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé that of spoken and school French.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in this file
alternatives: spans like the English ones (verses 2 and 7)
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the capitalised-pronoun setting has nothing to change. Nor are there gender spans on "የእስራኤል ልጆች" (verse 10) or on the generic "he" of verse 9, which in Amharic already take in women.

source.text: וַיִּדַּ֨ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל נֶ֛דֶר לַֽיהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אִם־נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֜ן אֶת־הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י וְהַֽחֲרַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־עָרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And vowed Israel [a] vow to Yahweh and said, If giving you will give the people the this into my hand, and I will devote to destruction their cities.

en.L: And Israel vowed a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will indeed give this people into my hand, then I will devote their cities to destruction."
en.B: Then Israel made a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will truly hand this people over to us, we will devote their towns to destruction."
en.R: Then Israel made a promise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They said, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} let us defeat these people, we will destroy their towns completely, as given over to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: Y Israel hizo un voto {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijo: «Si de cierto {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} entregas este pueblo en mi mano, yo consagraré sus ciudades a la destrucción».
es.B: Entonces Israel hizo un voto {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Si de veras {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos entregas a este pueblo, consagraremos sus poblados a la destrucción».
es.R: Entonces Israel hizo una promesa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Dijeron: «Si {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos dejas vencer a esta gente, destruiremos por completo sus poblados, como ofrenda consagrada a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}».

fr.L: Et Israël fit un vœu {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et dit : « Si vraiment {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} livres ce peuple entre mes mains, je vouerai leurs villes à la destruction. »
fr.B: Alors Israël fit un vœu {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous livres vraiment ce peuple, nous vouerons leurs villes à la destruction. »
fr.R: Alors Israël a fait une promesse {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Les Israélites ont dit : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous laisses vaincre ce peuple, nous détruirons complètement leurs villes, car elles {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} seront consacrées. »

sw.L: Naye Israeli akaweka nadhiri kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Ikiwa hakika utawatia watu hawa mkononi mwangu, basi nitaiweka wakfu miji yao kwa maangamizi."
sw.B: Ndipo Israeli wakaweka nadhiri kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: "Ikiwa kweli utawatia watu hawa mikononi mwetu, tutaiweka wakfu miji yao kwa maangamizi."
sw.R: Ndipo Waisraeli wakatoa ahadi kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wakasema, "Ukituwezesha kuwashinda watu hawa, tutaiangamiza kabisa miji yao, iwe wakfu kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}."

vi.L: Và Y-sơ-ra-ên khấn nguyện một lời khấn nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và nói: "Nếu Ngài thật sự phó dân này vào tay tôi, thì tôi sẽ tận diệt các thành của chúng."
vi.B: Bấy giờ Y-sơ-ra-ên khấn nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Nếu Ngài thật sự phó dân này vào tay chúng con, chúng con sẽ tận diệt các thành của họ."
vi.R: Bấy giờ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên hứa nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ nói: "Nếu Ngài cho chúng con thắng dân này, chúng con sẽ tiêu diệt hoàn toàn các thành của họ, như những vật đã dâng hết cho Ngài."

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 서원하여 말하였다. "주께서 이 백성을 정말로 내 손에 넘겨주시면, 내가 그들의 성읍들을 진멸하겠습니다."
ko.B: 그러자 이스라엘이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 서원했다. "주께서 이 백성을 정말로 우리에게 넘겨주시면, 우리가 그들의 성읍들을 진멸하겠습니다."
ko.R: 그러자 이스라엘이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 서원하며 말했다. "주께서 우리가 이 백성을 이기게 해 주시면, 우리가 그들의 성읍들을 주님께 바쳐 완전히 멸하겠습니다."

pt.L: E Israel fez um voto {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e disse: "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} de fato entregares este povo na minha mão, então votarei as suas cidades à destruição."
pt.B: Então Israel fez um voto {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} realmente entregares este povo em nossas mãos, consagraremos as suas cidades à destruição."
pt.R: Então Israel fez uma promessa {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. Eles disseram: "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nos deixares vencer este povo, vamos destruir completamente as suas cidades, como coisa entregue a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}."

am.L: እስራኤልም {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} ስእለት ተሳለ፤ እንዲህም አለ፦ «ይህን ሕዝብ በእጄ አሳልፈህ ብትሰጠኝ፣ ከተሞቻቸውን ለጥፋት እለያቸዋለሁ።»
am.B: ከዚያም እስራኤል {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} እንዲህ ብሎ ተሳለ፦ «ይህን ሕዝብ በእውነት በእጃችን አሳልፈህ ብትሰጠን፣ ከተሞቻቸውን ለጥፋት እንለያቸዋለን።»
am.R: ከዚያም እስራኤል {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} ቃል ገባ። እንዲህም አሉ፦ «እነዚህን ሰዎች ድል እንድናደርጋቸው ብትፈቅድልን፣ ከተሞቻቸውን ለአንተ የተሰጡ አድርገን ፈጽመን እናጠፋቸዋለን።»

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: give a whole town over to God, keeping nothing for themselves
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for a "devoted thing" in Leviticus 27:28-29: something given over to the LORD for good, which can never be bought back. In war it means the town and its people are destroyed and no plunder is taken for private use (Deuteronomy 20:16-18; Joshua 6:17-19). Israel promises not to fight this war for gain.

decisions.choice: if you will indeed give: a strong, emphatic condition
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the verb ("giving you will give"), which adds emphasis: "if you will really give". Israel asks God to give the victory and promises its part in return, as Jacob's vow does (Genesis 28:20-22).

decisions.choice: my hand, I will devote: Israel speaks as one person
decisions.reason: The whole nation is "Israel" and speaks in the singular, "my hand", "I will devote". The vow is the people's together. "Into my hand" means into my power.

decisions.choice: us, we
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "we" for the nation speaking as one, which English does not do with "I". Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: destroy their towns completely, as given over to you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words: the towns are destroyed because they are given over to God, not taken for gain. Literal and Balanced keep "devote to destruction". "Cities" in Literal; "towns" in Balanced and Readable, since these were small walled places.

decisions.choice: "tận diệt" (devote to destruction) at Literal and Balanced; Readable adds "như những vật đã dâng hết cho Ngài"
decisions.reason: "tận diệt" is the word the Vietnamese 1 Samuel 15 uses for the same Hebrew verb; Readable spells out, as the English does, that the towns are given over wholly to God.

decisions.choice: Israel praying: "Ngài" for God, "tôi" (Literal, the nation as one person) and "chúng con" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: People speaking to God say "con" / "chúng con" in prayer, as the Genesis sheet sets; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

decisions.choice: "진멸하다" (L, B); "주님께 바쳐 완전히 멸하다" (R) for devoting to destruction
decisions.reason: As Joshua in Korean: "진멸" is the term for giving a town wholly over to God; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Israel speaks to the LORD in the formal polite style (합쇼체), addressing him as "주께서"
decisions.reason: As people praying in Genesis and Psalms; Korean does not call God "당신".

decisions.choice: votar à destruição (L); consagrar à destruição (B); destruir completamente, como coisa entregue a ti (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one behind "anátema" in Leviticus 27:28 and 18:14 here (m1): the towns are given over to God, not taken for gain. Literal and Balanced keep both halves, the giving to God and the destruction; Readable says it in plain words, as the English Readable does. Verse 3 follows the same wording.

decisions.choice: "ለጥፋት መለየት" (devote to destruction) at Literal and Balanced; Readable "ለአንተ የተሰጡ አድርገን ፈጽመን እናጠፋቸዋለን"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch wording for *ḥerem* in war; Readable spells out, as the English Readable does, that the towns are given over to God, not kept as plunder.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה בְּק֣וֹל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וַיַּחֲרֵ֥ם אֶתְהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־עָרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א שֵׁם־הַמָּק֖וֹם חָרְמָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And listened Yahweh to [the] voice of Israel and gave the Canaanite[s], and he devoted to destruction them and their cities; and called [one] [the] name of the place Hormah.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to the voice of Israel and gave [over] the Canaanites, and [Israel] devoted them and their cities to destruction; and [one] called the name of the place Hormah.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} listened to Israel's plea and handed the Canaanites over, and Israel devoted them and their towns to destruction. So the place was named Hormah.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} listened to Israel and let them defeat the Canaanites. The Israelites destroyed them and their towns completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So that place was called Hormah, which means "Destruction."

es.L: Y escuchó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} la voz de Israel y entregó a los cananeos, y [Israel] los consagró a la destrucción a ellos y a sus ciudades; y [se] llamó el nombre del lugar Horma.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} escuchó la súplica de Israel y le entregó a los cananeos, e Israel los consagró a la destrucción, a ellos y a sus poblados. Por eso aquel lugar recibió el nombre de Horma.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} escuchó a Israel y le dio la victoria sobre los cananeos. Los israelitas los destruyeron por completo, a ellos y a sus poblados, como ofrenda consagrada {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Por eso aquel lugar se llamó Horma, que significa «Destrucción».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} écouta la voix d’Israël et livra les Cananéens, et [Israël] les voua à la destruction, eux et leurs villes ; et on appela le nom du lieu Horma.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} écouta la prière d’Israël et lui livra les Cananéens, et Israël les voua à la destruction, eux et leurs villes. C’est pourquoi on donna à ce lieu le nom de Horma.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a écouté Israël et lui a donné la victoire sur les Cananéens. Les Israélites les ont complètement détruits, eux et leurs villes, en les consacrant {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. C’est pourquoi on a appelé cet endroit Horma, ce qui veut dire « Destruction ».

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaisikiliza sauti ya Israeli, akawatoa Wakanaani, na [Israeli] akawaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi wao na miji yao; nalo jina la mahali pale likaitwa Horma.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyasikia maombi ya Israeli, akawatia Wakanaani mikononi mwao, nao Israeli wakawaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi wao pamoja na miji yao. Kwa hiyo mahali hapo paliitwa Horma.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwasikiliza Israeli, akawawezesha kuwashinda Wakanaani. Waisraeli waliwaangamiza kabisa wao pamoja na miji yao, kama vitu vilivyowekwa wakfu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kwa hiyo mahali hapo paliitwa Horma, maana yake "Maangamizi."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nghe tiếng Y-sơ-ra-ên và phó người Ca-na-an [cho họ], và [Y-sơ-ra-ên] tận diệt chúng và các thành của chúng; và [người ta] gọi tên nơi ấy là Họt-ma.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nghe lời cầu xin của Y-sơ-ra-ên và phó người Ca-na-an cho họ. Y-sơ-ra-ên tận diệt người Ca-na-an cùng các thành của chúng. Vì vậy nơi ấy được gọi là Họt-ma.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nghe lời dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và cho họ đánh thắng người Ca-na-an. Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên tiêu diệt hoàn toàn người Ca-na-an và các thành của họ, như những vật đã dâng hết cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Vì vậy nơi ấy được gọi là Họt-ma, nghĩa là "Tận Diệt".

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘의 목소리를 들으시고 가나안 사람을 넘겨주셨다. 그리고 [이스라엘이] 그들과 그들의 성읍들을 진멸하였다. 그리고 [사람들이] 그곳의 이름을 호르마라고 불렀다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘의 간청을 들으시고 가나안 사람들을 넘겨주셨다. 이스라엘은 그들과 그들의 성읍들을 진멸했다. 그래서 그곳의 이름을 호르마라고 했다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘의 기도를 들어주셔서, 그들이 가나안 사람들을 이기게 해 주셨다. 이스라엘 사람들은 그들과 그들의 성읍들을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바쳐 완전히 멸했다. 그래서 그곳은 '멸망'이라는 뜻의 호르마라고 불리게 되었다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ouviu a voz de Israel e entregou os cananeus, e [Israel] os votou à destruição, a eles e às suas cidades; e chamou-se o nome do lugar Hormá.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} ouviu o pedido de Israel e lhe entregou os cananeus, e Israel os consagrou à destruição, a eles e às suas cidades. Por isso o lugar recebeu o nome de Hormá.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} ouviu Israel e deixou que eles vencessem os cananeus. Os israelitas destruíram completamente os cananeus e as suas cidades, como coisa entregue {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. Por isso aquele lugar foi chamado Hormá, que quer dizer "Destruição".

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም የእስራኤልን ድምፅ ሰማ፤ ከነዓናውያንንም አሳልፎ ሰጠ፤ [እስራኤልም] እነርሱንና ከተሞቻቸውን ለጥፋት ለያቸው፤ የዚያንም ስፍራ ስም ሔርማ [ብለው] ጠሩት።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የእስራኤልን ልመና ሰምቶ ከነዓናውያንን አሳልፎ ሰጠ፤ እስራኤልም እነርሱንና ከተሞቻቸውን ለጥፋት ለያቸው። ስለዚህ ስፍራው ሔርማ ተባለ።
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የእስራኤልን ልመና ሰምቶ ከነዓናውያንን ድል እንዲያደርጓቸው ፈቀደላቸው። እስራኤላውያንም እነርሱንና ከተሞቻቸውን {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} የተሰጡ አድርገው ፈጽመው አጠፉ። ስለዚህ ያ ስፍራ ሔርማ ተባለ፤ ትርጉሙም «ጥፋት» ማለት ነው።

decisions.choice: Hormah: a name made from the same word as "devote to destruction"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the verb in this verse and verse 2, so it can be heard as "Destruction" or "Devoted place". It keeps the memory of the vow. Hormah was where Israel had been beaten back when they went up against the LORD's word (14:45); now, with the LORD's help, the same place sees their victory. Judges 1:17 tells of the naming of Hormah again, after Judah and Simeon destroyed Zephath.

decisions.choice: listened to the voice of Israel: granted what Israel asked
decisions.reason: "To listen to the voice" of someone here means to accept their request. The LORD answered the vow of verse 2.

decisions.choice: he devoted, one called: Israel did the destroying; the naming is impersonal
decisions.reason: "He devoted" has Israel, spoken of as one person, as its subject, as in verse 2. "He called" has no named subject and means "the place was called".

decisions.choice: [Israel] / Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he devoted". Naming Israel shows that it was the people, not the LORD, who carried out the vow.

decisions.choice: which means "Destruction"
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the name so that the reader can hear how it links with the vow.

decisions.choice: Readable gives the meaning of Hormah, «ጥፋት» (destruction); Balanced does not
alternatives: the meaning at Balanced too, as in Exodus 17:7
decisions.reason: The English Balanced has no explanation here, and the Amharic keeps the same quotations as the English level; Readable explains the name as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיִּסְע֞וּ מֵהֹ֤ר הָהָר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יַם־ס֔וּף לִסְבֹ֖ב אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֑וֹם וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נֶֽפֶשׁ־הָעָ֖ם בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from Hor the mountain [by the] way of [the] Sea of Reeds, to go around [the] land of Edom; and became short [the] soul of the people on the way.

en.L: And they set out from Hor the mountain by the way of the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Edom; and the soul of the people became short on the way.
en.B: They set out from Mount Hor along the road to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom, and on the way the people lost patience.
en.R: The Israelites left Mount Hor and went along the road toward the Red Sea, so that they could go around the country of Edom. But on the way the people became impatient.

es.L: Y partieron de Hor el monte, por el camino del mar de los Juncos, para rodear la tierra de Edom; y se acortó el alma del pueblo en el camino.
es.B: Partieron del monte Hor por el camino que lleva al mar Rojo, para rodear la tierra de Edom, y en el camino el pueblo perdió la paciencia.
es.R: Los israelitas salieron del monte Hor y fueron por el camino que va hacia el mar Rojo, para poder rodear el país de Edom. Pero en el camino el pueblo se impacientó.

fr.L: Et ils partirent de Hor la montagne par le chemin de la mer des Joncs, pour contourner le pays d’Édom ; et l’âme du peuple devint courte en chemin.
fr.B: Ils partirent du mont Hor par la route de la mer Rouge, pour contourner le pays d’Édom, et en chemin le peuple perdit patience.
fr.R: Les Israélites ont quitté le mont Hor et ont pris la route de la mer Rouge, pour faire le tour du pays d’Édom. Mais en chemin, le peuple s’est impatienté.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka Hori mlima kwa njia ya Bahari ya Matete, ili kuizunguka nchi ya Edomu; na nafsi ya watu ikawa fupi njiani.
sw.B: Walisafiri kutoka Mlima Hori kwa njia inayoelekea Bahari ya Shamu, ili kuizunguka nchi ya Edomu, na njiani watu wakakosa subira.
sw.R: Waisraeli waliondoka Mlima Hori, wakafuata njia inayoelekea Bahari ya Shamu, ili waweze kuizunguka nchi ya Edomu. Lakini njiani watu walikosa uvumilivu.

vi.L: Và họ nhổ trại từ núi Hô-rơ theo đường Biển Sậy, để đi vòng xứ Ê-đôm; và linh hồn của dân trở nên ngắn trên đường đi.
vi.B: Họ nhổ trại rời núi Hô-rơ, theo đường đi về phía Biển Đỏ để đi vòng quanh xứ Ê-đôm. Dọc đường, dân chúng mất kiên nhẫn.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên rời núi Hô-rơ và đi theo con đường về phía Biển Đỏ để đi vòng quanh xứ Ê-đôm. Nhưng dọc đường dân chúng trở nên nóng nảy.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 에돔 땅을 돌아가려고 호르 산에서 갈대 바다 길로 떠났다. 그리고 길에서 백성의 마음이 조급해졌다.
ko.B: 그들은 에돔 땅을 돌아가려고 호르 산을 떠나 홍해로 가는 길로 갔다. 그런데 백성은 길에서 참을성을 잃었다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 호르 산을 떠나 홍해 쪽으로 난 길을 따라갔다. 에돔 땅을 돌아서 가려고 한 것이다. 그런데 백성은 가는 길에 지쳐서 참을성을 잃었다.

pt.L: E partiram de Hor, o monte, pelo caminho do mar dos Juncos, para rodear a terra de Edom; e a alma do povo se encurtou no caminho.
pt.B: Eles partiram do monte Hor pelo caminho do mar Vermelho, para contornar a terra de Edom, e no caminho o povo perdeu a paciência.
pt.R: Os israelitas saíram do monte Hor e seguiram pelo caminho do mar Vermelho, para dar a volta na terra de Edom. Mas no caminho o povo ficou impaciente.

am.L: ከሖር ተራራም የኤዶምን ምድር ለመዞር በሸምበቆ ባሕር መንገድ ተጓዙ፤ የሕዝቡም ነፍስ በመንገድ ላይ አጠረች።
am.B: ከሖር ተራራ ተነሥተው የኤዶምን ምድር ለመዞር ወደ ቀይ ባሕር በሚወስደው መንገድ ሄዱ፤ በመንገድም ላይ ሕዝቡ ትዕግሥት አጡ።
am.R: እስራኤላውያን የኤዶምን አገር ዞረው ለማለፍ ከሖር ተራራ ተነሥተው ወደ ቀይ ባሕር በሚወስደው መንገድ ሄዱ። ነገር ግን በመንገድ ላይ ሕዝቡ ትዕግሥት አጡ።

decisions.choice: from Mount Hor, around Edom: the long way round
decisions.reason: Aaron had died on Mount Hor (20:22-29), and Edom had refused to let Israel pass through its land (20:14-21). So Israel had to go south and then around the edge of Edom, a long detour through hard country (Deuteronomy 2:1-8).

decisions.choice: the way of the Sea of Reeds: the road toward the gulf east of Sinai
decisions.reason: "Sea of Reeds" is the name used for the sea of the crossing (Exodus 13:18; 15:4), but it is also used for the gulf at Ezion-geber, east of the Sinai peninsula (1 Kings 9:26). Going around Edom, Israel headed south toward that gulf.

decisions.choice: the soul of the people became short: they lost patience and grew discouraged
decisions.reason: A "short soul" is the opposite of patience: people who cannot hold out any longer (Judges 10:16; 16:16). The long detour wore them down.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 13:18: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

decisions.choice: "갈대 바다" (L), "홍해" (B, R) for the Sea of Reeds
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Exodus to Deuteronomy: Literal keeps the Hebrew name where the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the familiar name, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Biển Sậy" (L); "Biển Đỏ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "the Sea of Reeds"; Literal says "Biển Sậy", as the Vietnamese Exodus and Joshua do, and Balanced and Readable keep the familiar name "Biển Đỏ".

decisions.choice: "linh hồn của dân trở nên ngắn" (the soul of the people became short) at Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means, that the people lost patience.

decisions.choice: "የሸምበቆ ባሕር" (Sea of Reeds) at Literal; "ቀይ ባሕር" (the Red Sea) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in Exodus in Amharic, following the English levels; the road ran toward the gulf east of Sinai (meaning decision m2).

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר הָעָ֗ם בֵּֽאלֹהִים֮ וּבְמֹשֶׁה֒ לָמָ֤ה הֶֽעֱלִיתֻ֨נוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לָמ֖וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְאֵ֣ין מַ֔יִם וְנַפְשֵׁ֣נוּ קָ֔צָה בַּלֶּ֖חֶם הַקְּלֹקֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke the people against God and against Moses, Why have you brought us up from Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread and there is no water, and our soul loathes the bread the worthless.

en.L: And the people spoke against God and against Moses, "Why have you brought us up from Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread and there is no water, and our soul loathes the worthless bread."
en.B: The people spoke against God and against Moses: "Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no food and no water, and we are sick of this pitiful food!"
en.R: The people complained against God and against Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt to die in this desert? There is no bread and no water. And we hate this awful food!"

es.L: Y habló el pueblo contra Dios y contra Moisés: «¿Por qué nos {{plural_you:han hecho subir|habéis hecho subir}} de Egipto para morir en el desierto? Porque no hay pan, y no hay agua, y nuestra alma aborrece este pan despreciable».
es.B: El pueblo habló contra Dios y contra Moisés: «¿Por qué nos {{plural_you:han sacado|habéis sacado}} de Egipto para morir en el desierto? ¡No hay comida ni agua, y ya estamos hartos de esta comida miserable!».
es.R: El pueblo se quejó contra Dios y contra Moisés. Decían: «¿Por qué nos {{plural_you:sacaron|sacasteis}} de Egipto para morir en este desierto? No hay pan ni agua. ¡Y odiamos esta comida horrible!».

fr.L: Et le peuple parla contre Dieu et contre Moïse : « Pourquoi nous avez-vous fait monter d’Égypte pour mourir dans le désert ? Car il n’y a pas de pain et il n’y a pas d’eau, et notre âme est dégoûtée de ce pain misérable. »
fr.B: Le peuple parla contre Dieu et contre Moïse : « Pourquoi nous avez-vous fait monter d’Égypte, pour que nous mourions dans le désert ? Il n’y a ni nourriture ni eau, et nous sommes écœurés de cette nourriture de misère ! »
fr.R: Le peuple s’est plaint contre Dieu et contre Moïse. Ils disaient : « Pourquoi nous avez-vous fait sortir d’Égypte pour mourir dans ce désert ? Il n’y a pas de pain, pas d’eau. Et nous détestons cette nourriture horrible ! »

sw.L: Nao watu wakanena dhidi ya Mungu na dhidi ya Musa, "Kwa nini mmetupandisha kutoka Misri ili tufe nyikani? Kwa maana hakuna mkate, wala hakuna maji, na nafsi yetu imechukizwa na mkate huu duni."
sw.B: Watu walinena dhidi ya Mungu na dhidi ya Musa: "Kwa nini mmetupandisha kutoka Misri ili tufe nyikani? Hakuna chakula wala maji, nasi tumechoshwa na chakula hiki duni!"
sw.R: Watu walilalamika dhidi ya Mungu na dhidi ya Musa. Walisema, "Kwa nini mlitutoa Misri ili tufe katika jangwa hili? Hakuna mkate wala maji. Na tunakichukia chakula hiki kibaya!"

vi.L: Và dân nói nghịch cùng Đức Chúa Trời và nghịch cùng Môi-se: "Tại sao các người đã đem chúng tôi lên khỏi Ai Cập để chết trong hoang mạc? Vì không có bánh và không có nước, và linh hồn chúng tôi ghê tởm thứ bánh tồi tệ này."
vi.B: Dân chúng nói nghịch với Đức Chúa Trời và với Môi-se: "Tại sao các người đem chúng tôi ra khỏi Ai Cập để chết trong hoang mạc? Không có bánh, cũng không có nước, và chúng tôi chán ngấy thứ đồ ăn khốn khổ này rồi!"
vi.R: Dân chúng phàn nàn nghịch với Đức Chúa Trời và với Môi-se. Họ nói: "Sao các người đem chúng tôi ra khỏi Ai Cập để chết trong hoang mạc này? Không có bánh, cũng không có nước. Chúng tôi ghét thứ đồ ăn tồi tệ này lắm rồi!"

ko.L: 그리고 백성이 하나님과 모세를 거슬러 말하였다. "어찌하여 우리를 이집트에서 올라오게 하여 광야에서 죽게 하십니까? 빵도 없고 물도 없습니다. 우리 영혼이 이 하찮은 빵을 몹시 싫어합니다."
ko.B: 백성이 하나님과 모세를 거슬러 말했다. "왜 우리를 이집트에서 이끌어 내어 이 광야에서 죽게 하십니까? 먹을 것도 없고 물도 없습니다. 이 형편없는 음식은 이제 지긋지긋합니다!"
ko.R: 백성이 하나님과 모세에게 불평했다. 그들이 말했다. "왜 우리를 이집트에서 데리고 나와서 이 광야에서 죽게 하십니까? 빵도 없고 물도 없습니다. 이 맛없는 음식은 이제 정말 싫습니다!"

pt.L: E o povo falou contra Deus e contra Moisés: "Por que vocês nos fizeram subir do Egito para morrermos no deserto? Pois não há pão e não há água, e a nossa alma tem nojo deste pão miserável."
pt.B: O povo falou contra Deus e contra Moisés: "Por que vocês nos fizeram subir do Egito para morrermos no deserto? Não há comida nem água, e estamos enjoados desta comida miserável!"
pt.R: O povo reclamou contra Deus e contra Moisés. Eles disseram: "Por que vocês nos tiraram do Egito para morrermos neste deserto? Não há pão nem água. E nós detestamos esta comida horrível!"

am.L: ሕዝቡም በእግዚአብሔርና በሙሴ ላይ እንዲህ ብለው ተናገሩ፦ «በምድረ በዳ እንድንሞት ከግብፅ ለምን አወጣችሁን? እንጀራ የለም፤ ውኃም የለም፤ ነፍሳችንም ይህን ዋጋ ቢስ እንጀራ ተጸየፈች።»
am.B: ሕዝቡ በእግዚአብሔርና በሙሴ ላይ እንዲህ ብለው ተናገሩ፦ «በምድረ በዳ እንድንሞት ከግብፅ ለምን አወጣችሁን? ምግብ የለም፤ ውኃም የለም፤ ይህም ዋጋ ቢስ ምግብ አስጠልቶናል!»
am.R: ሕዝቡ በእግዚአብሔርና በሙሴ ላይ አጉረመረሙ። እንዲህም አሉ፦ «በዚህ ምድረ በዳ እንድንሞት ከግብፅ ለምን አወጣችሁን? እንጀራ የለም፤ ውኃም የለም። ይህንንም አስጠሊታ ምግብ ጠላነው!»

decisions.choice: you have brought us up: plural, spoken to God and to Moses together
decisions.reason: "You" is plural. The people blame God and Moses at once, as the opening words of the verse say. Elsewhere the complaint is against Moses alone (20:4-5) or against God (14:2-3); here it is against both.

decisions.choice: no bread, worthless bread: no proper food, and the manna they despise
decisions.reason: The word means bread or food in general. They say there is none, and in the same breath they call the food they have "worthless": the manna, which they had already grown tired of (11:6). The complaint contradicts itself.

decisions.choice: worthless: contemptible, not worth anything
decisions.reason: The adjective is found only here. It comes from a root meaning "light" or "of little account", so it means food they treat as trash.

decisions.choice: our soul loathes: we are sick of it, we cannot stand it
decisions.reason: "Our soul" means "we ourselves", with a strong feeling of disgust (Genesis 27:46 uses the same verb).

decisions.choice: you, with no capitals
decisions.reason: This "you" is spoken to God and Moses together, so it is not written as a pronoun for God alone.

decisions.choice: "các người" (you, plural) for God and Moses together
decisions.reason: The people speak to God and Moses as one plural "you". Vietnamese has no neutral plural: "các người" is cold and disrespectful, which fits a complaint spoken against them, and, like the English, gives God no word of honour here.

decisions.choice: No pronoun for the plural "you"; the honorific "-십니까" carries it
decisions.reason: The complaint is spoken to God and Moses together; Korean leaves the subject unspoken rather than call God "당신".

decisions.choice: vocês (to God and Moses together), with no span
decisions.reason: The people speak to God and Moses at once with a plural "you" (m1). Portuguese has only "vocês" for that, though one addressed is God; it is not a pronoun for God alone, so it takes no setting, as in the English.

decisions.choice: Elohim is "እግዚአብሔር" here, and "አወጣችሁን" (you, plural)
decisions.reason: The one God is meant and the divine name does not stand beside it, so the Pentateuch terms give "እግዚአብሔር" (no divine_name span: it is not YHWH). The people speak to God and Moses together, so the verb is plural (meaning decision m1).

source.text: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח יְהוָ֜ה בָּעָ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַנְּחָשִׁ֣ים הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים וַֽיְנַשְּׁכ֖וּ אֶת־הָעָ֑ם וַיָּ֥מָת עַם־רָ֖ב מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Yahweh among the people the snakes the fiery [ones], and they bit the people; and died [a] people many from Israel.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent the fiery snakes among the people, and they bit the people; and many people of Israel died.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent fiery snakes among the people. They bit the people, and many Israelites died.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent fiery, poisonous snakes among the people. The snakes bit them, and many of the Israelites died.

es.L: Y envió {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entre el pueblo las serpientes ardientes, y mordieron al pueblo; y murió mucha gente de Israel.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} envió serpientes ardientes contra el pueblo. Mordieron a la gente, y murieron muchos israelitas.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mandó entre el pueblo serpientes ardientes y venenosas. Las serpientes los mordieron, y muchos israelitas murieron.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} envoya parmi le peuple les serpents brûlants, et ils mordirent le peuple ; et beaucoup de gens d’Israël moururent.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} envoya contre le peuple des serpents brûlants. Ils mordirent les gens, et beaucoup d’Israélites moururent.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a envoyé parmi le peuple des serpents brûlants et venimeux. Les serpents les ont mordus, et beaucoup d’Israélites sont morts.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akatuma kati ya watu nyoka wa moto, nao wakawauma watu; wakafa watu wengi wa Israeli.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akatuma nyoka wa moto kati ya watu. Nyoka hao wakawauma watu, na Waisraeli wengi wakafa.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alituma nyoka wa moto wenye sumu kati ya watu. Nyoka hao waliwauma, na Waisraeli wengi walikufa.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai những con rắn lửa vào giữa dân, và chúng cắn dân; và nhiều người trong Y-sơ-ra-ên chết.
vi.B: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai rắn lửa đến giữa dân chúng. Chúng cắn dân, và nhiều người Y-sơ-ra-ên chết.
vi.R: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai những con rắn độc, có nọc nóng như lửa, đến giữa dân chúng. Rắn cắn họ, và nhiều người Y-sơ-ra-ên chết.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 백성 가운데 불뱀들을 보내셨다. 그리고 그것들이 백성을 물었다. 그리고 이스라엘 가운데 많은 백성이 죽었다.
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 백성 가운데 불뱀들을 보내셨다. 뱀들이 백성을 물어서, 이스라엘 사람들이 많이 죽었다.
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 물리면 불에 덴 듯 아픈 독뱀들을 백성 가운데 보내셨다. 그 뱀들이 사람들을 물었고, 이스라엘 사람들 가운데 많은 사람이 죽었다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enviou entre o povo as serpentes abrasadoras, e elas morderam o povo; e morreu muita gente de Israel.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enviou serpentes abrasadoras contra o povo. Elas morderam o povo, e muitos israelitas morreram.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mandou cobras venenosas, de picada ardente, para o meio do povo. As cobras morderam o povo, e muitos israelitas morreram.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም እሳታማዎቹን እባቦች ወደ ሕዝቡ ላከ፤ ሕዝቡንም ነደፉ፤ ከእስራኤልም ብዙ ሕዝብ ሞተ።
am.B: ከዚያም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እሳታማ እባቦችን ወደ ሕዝቡ ላከ። እባቦቹ ሕዝቡን ነደፉ፤ ከእስራኤላውያንም ብዙዎች ሞቱ።
am.R: ከዚያም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የሚያቃጥል መርዝ ያላቸውን እባቦች ወደ ሕዝቡ ላከ። እባቦቹ ነደፉአቸው፤ ከእስራኤላውያንም ብዙዎቹ ሞቱ።

decisions.choice: the fiery snakes: snakes whose bite burned, or whose color looked like fire
decisions.reason: The word added to "snakes" comes from the verb "to burn". It may describe the burning pain and fever of their poison, or a fiery color. The same word names a flying serpent in Isaiah 14:29 and 30:6, and the winged beings around God's throne in Isaiah 6:2. Deuteronomy 8:15 remembers the wilderness as a land of "fiery snakes and scorpions".

decisions.choice: the LORD sent: punishment for speaking against him
decisions.reason: The snakes come as God's answer to the people's words against him and his gift of food (verse 5). Paul recalls this event as a warning (1 Corinthians 10:9).

decisions.choice: fiery, poisonous snakes
decisions.reason: Readable adds "poisonous", since the snakes' bite killed many (this verse), whatever "fiery" refers to.

decisions.choice: serpientes ardientes
decisions.reason: "Serpiente", not the "culebra" used for the staff in Exodus 7, since this is the familiar name of the event ("la serpiente de bronce", verse 9). "Ardientes" keeps the Hebrew image of burning; Readable adds "venenosas" as the English does.

decisions.choice: des serpents brûlants
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to burn", whether it means the burning bite or a fiery colour; "brûlants" keeps that image. Readable adds "venimeux" as the English adds "poisonous".

decisions.choice: nyoka wa moto
decisions.reason: "Wa moto" (of fire) keeps the Hebrew picture of burning, which verse 8 uses again for the figure Moses makes. Readable adds "wenye sumu" (poisonous) as the English does.

decisions.choice: "rắn lửa" (fiery snakes) at Literal and Balanced; Readable "rắn độc, có nọc nóng như lửa"
decisions.reason: Keeps the Hebrew "fiery" without deciding whether it is the burning bite or the colour; Readable adds "poisonous" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "불뱀" (L, B); "물리면 불에 덴 듯 아픈 독뱀" (R) for the fiery snakes
decisions.reason: "불뱀" keeps the Hebrew picture; Readable explains it, as the English Readable adds "poisonous".

decisions.choice: as serpentes abrasadoras (L, B); cobras venenosas, de picada ardente (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter. "Abrasador" comes, like the Hebrew, from burning, and leaves open whether the bite or the color burned (m1). Literal and Balanced say "serpente", as John 3:14 does at those levels for the bronze figure of verse 9, so the link Jesus draws is heard; Readable says "cobra", the everyday word used for the same Hebrew word in Exodus 4:3, and as John 3:14 Readable says "uma cobra de bronze". Readable adds "venenosas" as the English Readable adds "poisonous".

decisions.choice: "እሳታማ እባቦች" (fiery snakes); Readable "የሚያቃጥል መርዝ ያላቸው እባቦች"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls them by the word for burning; Literal and Balanced keep the picture, Readable says what it means for the bite, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיָּבֹא֩ הָעָ֨ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ חָטָ֗אנוּ כִּֽי־דִבַּ֤רְנוּ בַֽיהוָה֙ וָבָ֔ךְ הִתְפַּלֵּל֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְיָסֵ֥ר מֵעָלֵ֖ינוּ אֶת־הַנָּחָ֑שׁ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came the people to Moses and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against Yahweh and against you; pray to Yahweh, and may he take away from on us the snake; and prayed Moses on behalf of the people.

en.L: And the people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned, for we have spoken against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and against you. Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may take away the snakes from us." And Moses prayed for the people.
en.B: The people came to Moses and said, "We sinned when we spoke against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and against you. Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
en.R: The people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned. We spoke against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and against you. Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.

es.L: Y vino el pueblo a Moisés y dijeron: «Hemos pecado, porque hemos hablado contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y contra ti. Ora {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, para que quite de nosotros las serpientes». Y oró Moisés por el pueblo.
es.B: El pueblo fue a Moisés y le dijo: «Pecamos al hablar contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y contra ti. Ruega {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} que aparte de nosotros las serpientes». Así que Moisés oró por el pueblo.
es.R: La gente fue a ver a Moisés y le dijo: «Hemos pecado. Hablamos contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y contra ti. Ora {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y pídele que nos quite las serpientes». Entonces Moisés oró por el pueblo.

fr.L: Et le peuple vint à Moïse et dit : « Nous avons péché, car nous avons parlé contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et contre toi. Prie {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} éloigne de nous les serpents. » Et Moïse pria pour le peuple.
fr.B: Le peuple vint trouver Moïse et dit : « Nous avons péché en parlant contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et contre toi. Prie {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} d’éloigner de nous ces serpents. » Moïse pria donc pour le peuple.
fr.R: Les gens sont venus voir Moïse et lui ont dit : « Nous avons péché. Nous avons parlé contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et contre toi. Prie {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et demande-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} d’éloigner de nous les serpents. » Alors Moïse a prié pour le peuple.

sw.L: Nao watu wakamjia Musa, wakasema, "Tumefanya dhambi, kwa kuwa tumenena dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na dhidi yako. Umwombe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ili atuondolee nyoka." Naye Musa akawaombea watu.
sw.B: Watu walimjia Musa, wakasema, "Tulitenda dhambi tuliponena dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na dhidi yako. Mwombe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atuondolee nyoka hawa." Basi Musa akawaombea watu.
sw.R: Watu walikuja kwa Musa, wakasema, "Tumefanya dhambi. Tulinena dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na dhidi yako. Mwombe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umsihi atuondolee nyoka hawa." Basi Musa akawaombea watu.

vi.L: Và dân đến với Môi-se và nói: "Chúng tôi đã phạm tội, vì chúng tôi đã nói nghịch cùng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và nghịch cùng ông. Xin ông cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cất rắn khỏi chúng tôi." Và Môi-se cầu nguyện cho dân.
vi.B: Dân chúng đến với Môi-se và nói: "Chúng tôi đã phạm tội khi nói nghịch với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và với ông. Xin ông cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cất rắn khỏi chúng tôi." Vậy Môi-se cầu nguyện cho dân chúng.
vi.R: Dân chúng đến với Môi-se và nói: "Chúng tôi đã phạm tội. Chúng tôi đã nói nghịch với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và với ông. Xin ông cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đem rắn đi khỏi chúng tôi." Vậy Môi-se cầu nguyện cho dân chúng.

ko.L: 그리고 백성이 모세에게 와서 말하였다. "우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 당신을 거슬러 말하였으니 죄를 지었습니다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도하여, 그분께서 우리에게서 그 뱀을 없애 주시게 하십시오." 그리고 모세가 백성을 위하여 기도하였다.
ko.B: 백성이 모세에게 와서 말했다. "우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 당신을 거슬러 말하여 죄를 지었습니다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도하여 뱀들이 우리에게서 떠나가게 해 주십시오." 그래서 모세가 백성을 위하여 기도했다.
ko.R: 백성이 모세에게 와서 말했다. "우리가 죄를 지었습니다. 우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 당신을 원망하는 말을 했습니다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도하여 그 뱀들을 우리에게서 없애 달라고 해 주십시오." 그래서 모세가 백성을 위하여 기도했다.

pt.L: E o povo veio a Moisés e disse: "Pecamos, porque falamos contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} e contra você. Ore {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tire de nós as serpentes." E Moisés orou pelo povo.
pt.B: O povo veio a Moisés e disse: "Pecamos quando falamos contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} e contra você. Ore {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} para que tire de nós as serpentes." Então Moisés orou pelo povo.
pt.R: O povo foi até Moisés e disse: "Nós pecamos. Falamos contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} e contra você. Ore {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e peça a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} que tire as cobras do meio de nós." Então Moisés orou pelo povo.

am.L: ሕዝቡም ወደ ሙሴ መጥተው እንዲህ አሉ፦ «{{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ላይና በአንተ ላይ ተናግረናልና ኃጢአት ሠርተናል፤ እባቡን ከእኛ ላይ እንዲያነሣልን {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} ጸልይ።» ሙሴም ስለ ሕዝቡ ጸለየ።
am.B: ሕዝቡ ወደ ሙሴ መጥተው «{{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ላይና በአንተ ላይ በመናገራችን ኃጢአት ሠርተናል። እባቦቹን ከእኛ እንዲያርቅልን {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} ጸልይ» አሉት። ስለዚህ ሙሴ ስለ ሕዝቡ ጸለየ።
am.R: ሕዝቡ ወደ ሙሴ መጥተው እንዲህ አሉ፦ «ኃጢአት ሠርተናል። {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ላይና በአንተ ላይ ተናግረናል። እባቦቹን ከእኛ እንዲያርቅልን {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} ጸልይ፤ ለምነውም።» ስለዚህ ሙሴ ስለ ሕዝቡ ጸለየ።

decisions.choice: we have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD: the people admit their complaint was sin
decisions.reason: The people repeat the words of verse 5 ("spoke against") and name them as sin, against the LORD first and then against Moses. They ask the one they blamed to pray for them.

decisions.choice: the snake: one word standing for all the snakes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the singular, "the snake", used for the whole kind, as in verse 6 where the plural is used.

decisions.choice: prayed for: prayed on behalf of
decisions.reason: Moses stands between the people and God, as he did before (11:2; 14:13-19). God answers, though not by removing the snakes (verse 8).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ שָׂרָ֔ף וְשִׂ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ עַל־נֵ֑ס וְהָיָה֙ כָּל־הַנָּשׁ֔וּךְ וְרָאָ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ וָחָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, Make for yourself [a] fiery [one] and set it on [a] pole; and it will be [that] every one bitten, and he sees it, and he will live.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Make for yourself a fiery [snake] and set it on a pole; and it will be [that] everyone who is bitten and sees it will live."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Make a fiery snake and put it up on a pole. Anyone who is bitten can look at it and live."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Make a model of a fiery snake and put it on top of a pole. Anyone who has been bitten can look at it and stay alive."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés: «Hazte una [serpiente] ardiente y ponla sobre un asta; y será [que] todo el que sea mordido y la mire, vivirá».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «Haz una serpiente ardiente y colócala en lo alto de un asta. Todo el que sea mordido podrá mirarla y vivirá».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Haz la figura de una serpiente ardiente y ponla en la punta de un palo. Cualquiera que haya sido mordido podrá mirarla y seguir con vida».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Fais-toi un [serpent] brûlant et place-le sur une perche ; et il arrivera [que] quiconque aura été mordu et le regardera vivra. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Fabrique un serpent brûlant et dresse-le sur une perche. Quiconque aura été mordu pourra le regarder et vivre. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Fais la figure d’un serpent brûlant et mets-la en haut d’une perche. Toute personne mordue pourra la regarder, et elle restera en vie. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Jifanyie [nyoka] wa moto, ukamweke juu ya nguzo; na itakuwa [kwamba] kila aliyeumwa, akimtazama, ataishi."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Tengeneza nyoka wa moto, umtundike juu ya nguzo. Mtu yeyote aliyeumwa anaweza kumtazama, naye ataishi."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Tengeneza sanamu ya nyoka wa moto, uiweke juu ya nguzo. Mtu yeyote aliyeumwa na nyoka anaweza kuitazama, naye atabaki hai."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy làm cho ngươi một [con rắn] lửa và đặt nó trên một cây sào; và [sẽ xảy ra là] mọi người bị cắn mà nhìn nó thì sẽ sống."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy làm một con rắn lửa và treo nó lên một cây sào. Ai bị cắn mà nhìn lên nó thì sẽ được sống."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy làm hình một con rắn lửa và đặt nó trên đầu một cây sào. Ai bị rắn cắn mà nhìn lên nó thì sẽ được sống."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "너를 위하여 불[뱀]을 만들어 장대 위에 달아라. 그러면 물린 사람은 누구든지 그것을 보면 살 것이다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "불뱀을 만들어 장대 위에 달아 놓아라. 뱀에게 물린 사람은 누구든지 그것을 쳐다보면 살 것이다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "불뱀 모양을 하나 만들어서 장대 꼭대기에 달아라. 뱀에게 물린 사람은 누구든지 그것을 쳐다보면 죽지 않고 살 것이다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Faze para ti uma [serpente] abrasadora e põe-na sobre uma haste; e será [que] todo aquele que for mordido e olhar para ela viverá."
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Faze uma serpente abrasadora e coloca-a no alto de uma haste. Quem for mordido poderá olhar para ela e viverá."
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Faze a figura de uma cobra venenosa e põe essa figura no alto de um poste. Quem tiver sido mordido pode olhar para ela e continuar vivo."

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም ሙሴን አለው፦ «እሳታማ [እባብ] ሥራልህ፤ በዘንግም ላይ አድርገው፤ የተነደፈም ሁሉ ቢያየው በሕይወት ይኖራል።»
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሙሴን እንዲህ አለው፦ «እሳታማ እባብ ሠርተህ በዘንግ ላይ ከፍ አድርገህ አኑረው። የተነደፈ ማንኛውም ሰው ቢያየው በሕይወት ይኖራል።»
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሙሴን እንዲህ አለው፦ «የእሳታማ እባብ ምስል ሠርተህ በዘንግ ጫፍ ላይ አድርገው። የተነደፈ ማንኛውም ሰው ቢመለከተው በሕይወት ይኖራል።»

decisions.choice: a fiery one: a figure of the fiery snake
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "a fiery [one]", using the word that described the snakes in verse 6 on its own. Verse 9 shows that it was a snake made of bronze.

decisions.choice: a pole: a tall pole raised as a signal
decisions.reason: The word is used of a pole or standard set up where everyone can see it, often as a rallying sign (Isaiah 5:26; 11:12). Moses' altar was named "The LORD is my banner" with the same word (Exodus 17:15).

decisions.choice: sees it and lives: healing comes from God by trusting his word
decisions.reason: The figure does not heal by itself; God gives life to those who do what he said and look. Later, when the people burned incense to this bronze snake, King Hezekiah broke it in pieces (2 Kings 18:4). Jesus compares his own lifting up to it (John 3:14-15).

decisions.choice: a model of a fiery snake
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Moses is to make an image, not a living snake.

decisions.choice: un asta (L, B); un palo (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a pole raised high as a signal. "Asta" is a tall pole for raising something into view; Readable uses the everyday "palo". "Estandarte" would suggest a flag.

decisions.choice: uma haste (L, B); um poste (R)
decisions.reason: The word names a pole raised where all can see it (m2). "Haste" is the pole of a flag or standard; "vara" is kept for the staffs of chapter 17. Readable says "poste", as John 3:14 Readable does ("num poste").

decisions.choice: "ዘንግ" (pole) and "እባብ" (snake), with "ከፍ አድርገህ" (lift it up) at Balanced
decisions.reason: John 3:14 in Amharic recalls this verse: Moses "lifted up" ("ከፍ አደረገ") the serpent, and Readable there sets the bronze snake "on a pole" ("በዘንግ ላይ"). The Hebrew agrees, so the words are kept; "ሰቀለ" is avoided, as there.

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ מֹשֶׁה֙ נְחַ֣שׁ נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וַיְשִׂמֵ֖הוּ עַל־הַנֵּ֑ס וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־נָשַׁ֤ךְ הַנָּחָשׁ֙ אֶת־אִ֔ישׁ וְהִבִּ֛יט אֶל־נְחַ֥שׁ הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת וָחָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And made Moses [a] snake of bronze and set it on the pole; and it was [that] if had bitten the snake [a] man, and he looked to [the] snake of the bronze, and he lived.

en.L: And Moses made a snake of bronze and set it on the pole; and it was [that] if the snake had bitten anyone, and {{gender:they|he}} looked to the snake of bronze, {{gender:they|he}} lived.
en.B: So Moses made a bronze snake and set it on the pole. Whenever a snake had bitten someone, and that person looked at the bronze snake, they lived.
en.R: So Moses made a snake out of bronze and put it on the pole. After that, whenever a snake bit someone, that person could look at the bronze snake and stay alive.

es.L: E hizo Moisés una serpiente de bronce y la puso sobre el asta; y sucedía [que] si la serpiente había mordido a alguien, y esa persona miraba a la serpiente de bronce, vivía.
es.B: Moisés hizo, pues, una serpiente de bronce y la puso sobre el asta. Cada vez que una serpiente mordía a alguien y esa persona miraba la serpiente de bronce, vivía.
es.R: Entonces Moisés hizo una serpiente de bronce y la puso en el palo. Desde entonces, cuando una serpiente mordía a alguien, esa persona podía mirar la serpiente de bronce y seguir con vida.

fr.L: Et Moïse fit un serpent de bronze et le plaça sur la perche ; et il arrivait [que], si le serpent avait mordu quelqu’un et que cette personne regardait vers le serpent de bronze, elle vivait.
fr.B: Moïse fit donc un serpent de bronze et le plaça sur la perche. Chaque fois qu’un serpent avait mordu quelqu’un et que cette personne regardait le serpent de bronze, elle vivait.
fr.R: Alors Moïse a fait un serpent en bronze et l’a mis sur la perche. Depuis, quand un serpent mordait quelqu’un, cette personne pouvait regarder le serpent de bronze et rester en vie.

sw.L: Naye Musa akafanya nyoka wa shaba, akamweka juu ya nguzo; ikawa, nyoka alipokuwa amemwuma mtu, naye akamtazama yule nyoka wa shaba, akaishi.
sw.B: Basi Musa akatengeneza nyoka wa shaba, akamweka juu ya nguzo. Kila mara nyoka alipomwuma mtu, na mtu huyo akamtazama yule nyoka wa shaba, aliishi.
sw.R: Basi Musa alitengeneza nyoka kwa shaba, akamweka juu ya nguzo. Tangu hapo, nyoka alipomwuma mtu, mtu huyo aliweza kumtazama yule nyoka wa shaba, akabaki hai.

vi.L: Và Môi-se làm một con rắn bằng đồng và đặt nó trên cây sào; và [xảy ra là] nếu rắn đã cắn người nào, và người ấy nhìn lên con rắn bằng đồng, thì người ấy sống.
vi.B: Vậy Môi-se làm một con rắn bằng đồng và đặt nó trên cây sào. Hễ ai bị rắn cắn mà nhìn lên con rắn bằng đồng, người ấy được sống.
vi.R: Vậy Môi-se làm một con rắn bằng đồng và đặt nó trên cây sào. Từ đó, mỗi khi có ai bị rắn cắn, người ấy có thể nhìn lên con rắn bằng đồng và được sống.

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 놋으로 뱀을 만들어 그것을 장대 위에 달았다. 그리고 뱀이 어떤 사람을 물었을 때, 그 사람이 놋뱀을 쳐다보면 살았다.
ko.B: 그래서 모세는 놋뱀을 만들어 장대 위에 달아 놓았다. 뱀에게 물린 사람은 누구든지 그 놋뱀을 쳐다보면 살아났다.
ko.R: 그래서 모세는 놋으로 뱀을 만들어 장대 위에 달았다. 그 뒤로는 누가 뱀에게 물려도, 그 사람이 놋뱀을 쳐다보면 죽지 않고 살았다.

pt.L: E Moisés fez uma serpente de bronze e a pôs sobre a haste; e acontecia [que], se a serpente mordia alguém, e este olhava para a serpente de bronze, vivia.
pt.B: Então Moisés fez uma serpente de bronze e a colocou na haste. Sempre que uma serpente mordia alguém, e essa pessoa olhava para a serpente de bronze, ela vivia.
pt.R: Então Moisés fez uma cobra de bronze e a pôs no poste. Depois disso, sempre que uma cobra mordia alguém, a pessoa podia olhar para a cobra de bronze e continuava viva.

am.L: ሙሴም የነሐስ እባብ ሠርቶ በዘንጉ ላይ አደረገው፤ እባብም ሰውን በነደፈው ጊዜ የነሐሱን እባብ ቢመለከት በሕይወት ይኖር ነበር።
am.B: ስለዚህ ሙሴ የነሐስ እባብ ሠርቶ በዘንጉ ላይ አደረገው። እባብ ማንንም በነደፈ ጊዜ ያ ሰው የነሐሱን እባብ ቢመለከት በሕይወት ይኖር ነበር።
am.R: ስለዚህ ሙሴ ከነሐስ እባብ ሠርቶ በዘንጉ ላይ አደረገው። ከዚያ በኋላ እባብ አንድን ሰው በነደፈ ጊዜ ያ ሰው የነሐሱን እባብ ተመልክቶ በሕይወት ይኖር ነበር።

decisions.choice: a snake of bronze: a play on two words that sound alike
decisions.reason: "Snake" (nachash) and "bronze" (nechoshet) sound alike in Hebrew. Bronze, a mix of copper and tin, can also shine with a reddish color like the "fiery" snakes.

decisions.choice: if ... and he looked ... and he lived: whenever this happened
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe something that kept happening: each time a person was bitten and looked, that person lived. The bronze snake stayed with Israel until Hezekiah's day (2 Kings 18:4).

decisions.choice: a man: anyone, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word often means "a man", but here it means any person the snakes bit.

decisions.choice: alguien ... esa persona
decisions.reason: The English has a gender setting (they/he) for the person bitten. "Esa persona" covers a man or a woman, and Spanish needs no pronoun after it, so no setting span is needed.

decisions.choice: quelqu'un ... cette personne ... elle
decisions.reason: The English has a gender setting (they/he) for the person bitten. "Cette personne" covers a man or a woman in one natural wording, so the French needs no setting span.

decisions.choice: "người nào ... người ấy" (anyone ... that person), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" covers man or woman, as the meaning decision reads the Hebrew "a man".

decisions.choice: "놋뱀" for the snake of bronze, with no gender span for "he" ("그 사람")
decisions.reason: "놋" is the word for bronze settled for the tabernacle in Exodus; "그 사람" already includes men and women, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: alguém, e este olhava ... vivia (no span)
decisions.reason: Where the English Literal puts the pronoun under the gender setting, Portuguese says "alguém" and refers back to it with "este" and the verb alone, which already mean anyone (style section 7), so no span is needed.

decisions.choice: "የነሐስ እባብ" (bronze snake), as John 3:14 in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on two words that sound alike (meaning decision m1); Amharic cannot echo it and keeps the plain words the New Testament uses. The generic "he" of "ቢመለከት" takes in anyone, so the English gender span has no Amharic counterpart.

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun: on the east
decisions.reason: "The rising of the sun" is the east. The camp was in the wilderness at Moab's eastern edge, still outside Moab's farmland (Deuteronomy 2:8).

decisions.choice: the wadi of Zered: a stream valley on Moab's southern side
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley with a stream that often runs only in the rainy season. The Zered flows west into the south end of the Dead Sea and divided Edom from Moab. Deuteronomy 2:13-14 marks crossing it as the end of the thirty-eight years of wandering.

decisions.choice: the Zered Valley
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "wadi"; Balanced and Readable use "valley", the plain English word, here and in verses 14, 15 and 20.

decisions.choice: "khe" (wadi) at Literal, "thung lũng" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: A wadi is a stream bed that is dry most of the year; Literal keeps "khe" as the Hebrew "naḥal", the others say "valley" as the English does. The same in 21:14-15.

decisions.choice: "시내" (L), "골짜기" (B, R) for the wadi (nahal)
decisions.reason: A wadi is a stream valley that runs only in the rainy season; Literal keeps the stream, Balanced and Readable the valley, as the English does.

decisions.choice: o uádi (L); o vale (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps "uádi", the Portuguese word for a stream valley that runs only in the rainy season (m1); Balanced and Readable say "vale", here and in verses 14, 15 and 20.

decisions.choice: the Book of the Wars of the LORD: a lost collection of songs
decisions.reason: This book is named only here. It was probably a collection of poems about the battles the LORD fought for Israel, like the Book of Jashar (Joshua 10:13; 2 Samuel 1:18). Only these few lines survive, quoted to show that the Arnon valleys belonged to Moab's border (verse 13).

decisions.choice: Waheb ... and the wadis: the quotation begins in the middle of a sentence
decisions.reason: The Hebrew marks "Waheb" and "the wadis" as objects of a verb, but the verb is not quoted. The lines may have said something like "he took" or "we passed" Waheb. The quotation is a fragment, and its main verb cannot be known.

decisions.choice: Waheb in Suphah: two places, neither of them known today
decisions.reason: Both are read as place names near the Arnon. "Suphah" may also be a common word, "storm" or "whirlwind", which would give "Waheb in a storm", perhaps a picture of the LORD coming in battle.

decisions.choice: valleys
decisions.reason: As in verse 12: Literal keeps "wadis"; Balanced and Readable use "valleys".

decisions.choice: makorongo ya Arnoni (L); mabonde (B, R)
decisions.reason: A wadi here is the deep gorge of the Arnon and its side valleys, so Literal uses "makorongo" (ravines) rather than "vijito" (streams); Balanced and Readable use "mabonde" (valleys), as the English uses "valleys".

decisions.choice: then Israel sang: the words used of the song at the sea
decisions.reason: "Then ... sang" is how the song of Moses begins after the crossing of the sea (Exodus 15:1). Here Israel sings again, over water in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: spring up, well; sing to it: the well is spoken to, then the people
decisions.reason: "Spring up" is said to the well, as if calling the water to rise. "Sing" is said to the people. The song may have been sung while digging or drawing water.

decisions.choice: sing to it: sing in answer to it, sing about it
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to answer or to sing in turns; with "to it" it means to sing over the well, greeting the water.

decisions.choice: Bubble up
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for water rising from the ground.

decisions.choice: Brota (tu, to the well); Cantem (vocês, to the people)
decisions.reason: The song speaks to the well, as a poem may speak to a thing, with the second person singular, and then to the singers in the plural (m2); Portuguese keeps both persons and, by the style rules, uses "vocês" for the plural, never "vós".

decisions.choice: "በዚያን ጊዜ ... ይህን መዝሙር ዘመረ" (then ... sang this song)
decisions.reason: The opening words of the Song of the Sea in Exodus 15:1 in Amharic, which this verse echoes (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: princes, nobles of the people: the leading men
decisions.reason: The two words stand in parallel for the people's chief men. That they dig with their staffs of office may be a way of saying the well was opened by their command, a ceremony rather than hard digging.

decisions.choice: scepter, staffs: the rods that marked leaders
decisions.reason: The first word means a ruler's staff or one who decrees (Genesis 49:10). The second is a staff to lean on. Leaders carried such staffs as signs of their authority (17:17-18).

decisions.choice: Mattanah: a place whose name means "gift"
decisions.reason: Mattanah is a stage on the journey, not known today. The name sounds like the word for a gift, fitting after the gift of water, but the text does not draw that link.

decisions.choice: the end of the quotation before "from the wilderness"
decisions.reason: The song ends with "their staffs"; the last words go back to the list of stages begun in verse 16. The quotation marks close before them.

decisions.choice: Leaders dug this well.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the song's opening into a full sentence. Its breaks follow the Hebrew lines, one fewer than Literal.

decisions.choice: os seus cajados
decisions.reason: This is a staff to lean on, a different Hebrew word from the "vara" of chapter 17 (m2); "cajado" is the walking staff, so the two words stay apart in Portuguese.

decisions.choice: Pisgah: the ridge at the edge of the high plateau, above the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Pisgah is the height from which Moses later saw the promised land before he died (Deuteronomy 3:27; 34:1). Balaam is taken there in 23:14.

decisions.choice: the Jeshimon: the wasteland, the desert by the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The word means "desert" or "wasteland" and is used as the name of the barren land on the Dead Sea's shores (23:28; 1 Samuel 23:19).

decisions.choice: the field of Moab: the open country of Moab
decisions.reason: "Field" here means the open country or territory of a people, as "the field of Edom" in Genesis 32:4. This was land Moab had once held, north of the Arnon (verse 26).

decisions.choice: From there you can look down
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that Pisgah "looks down" on the wasteland. Readable makes the picture of the view plain.
